Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-LjvfDb on main, reviewing PLAN.md (pricing tier).
ELI10: gstack has a dozen skills (/office-hours, /ship, /investigate...). A short routing table in CLAUDE.md tells Claude which one to reach for when you say things like 'this is broken' or 'ship it', so you don't have to remember slash names. Without it, you invoke skills by hand.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Low either way. Miss out on auto-routing, or get a ~15-line block in CLAUDE.md you didn't want.
Recommendation: A because auto-routing is the default gstack experience and the block is small and reversible.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.

options.label: Add routing rules to CLAUDE.md (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Natural-language requests ('fix this bug', 'review scope') route to the right skill automatically
✅ One-time setup; the block is ~15 lines and trivially deletable

questions.question:
D2 — No design doc found. Run /office-hours first, or proceed with the standard review?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-LjvfDb on main, reviewing PLAN.md (pricing tier).
ELI10: /office-hours is a structured 'what problem are we really solving' session: problem statement, premise challenge, explored alternatives. It produces a design doc this review can lean on. Your plan already admits its premise is untested (nobody has talked to developers), which is exactly what /office-hours is built to sharpen. Takes ~10 minutes.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Skip it and the review challenges the premise itself, but with thinner input. Run it and you spend 10 minutes before the review starts.
Recommendation: A because this plan is 3 lines with an unvalidated premise; the review will spend most of its time on premise anyway, and /office-hours does that better.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: 10 minutes of upfront problem framing vs. jumping straight into review of a plan that mostly lacks a problem statement.

options.label: Run /office-hours now (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Produces a problem statement and alternatives the review can grade against, not just the 3-line PLAN.md
✅ Directly addresses the plan's own admitted gap: no developer input, no evidence pricing is the barrier
❌ ~10 minutes of Q&A before the review starts (human: ~10 min / CC: ~10 min, it's conversational)

options.label: Skip — proceed with standard review
options.description:
✅ Review starts immediately; Step 0 premise challenge still runs at full depth
✅ Fine if you already have the problem framing in your head and just want the critique
❌ Review works from a 3-line plan; more findings will be 'unknown, go find out' rather than concrete

questions.question:
D3 — Enable cross-project learnings search?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-LjvfDb on main, reviewing PLAN.md (pricing tier).
ELI10: gstack logs small lessons per project (command quirks, pitfalls). With this on, reviews can also search lessons from your other projects on this machine. Everything stays local; nothing leaves your machine. Good for solo devs; skip if you work across client codebases where mixing context is a concern.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Low. Either miss a few reusable lessons, or see a lesson from an unrelated codebase.
Recommendation: A because it is local-only and the current project has zero learnings, so any signal has to come from elsewhere.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: more recall vs. strict project isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project learnings (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Reviews can apply patterns already learned on your other local projects
✅ Local only; no data leaves the machine, and it can be turned off any time
❌ A lesson from an unrelated codebase could surface where it doesn't apply

options.label: Keep learnings project-scoped only
options.description:
✅ Strict isolation between codebases; nothing from client A shows up in client B
✅ Zero chance of a misapplied cross-project pattern
❌ This project has 0 learnings today, so the search returns nothing until some accumulate
